en: Holding a book, a mudrā, a rosary, and a jar of nectar in her hands, radiant as ten million suns, she who is the consort of the Lotus-born One, bestowing all that is desired upon the multitude of beings who bow before her;
she who is worshipped by Indra, Upendra, and others; the mother of the three worlds; the progenitor of speech; the refuge.
May this venerable Śāradāmbā, who bestows all happiness, grant auspicious blessings.
Thus ends the meditation.
Upon that most pure seat situated on the banks of the Tuṅgā river in the city named Śṛṅgerī, established by the illustrious Śaṅkara, the lord of teachers, and frequented by noble sages—
I behold Śivā, shining intensely with a splendor equal to ten million suns.
I ever revere Śāradā, whose lotus-eyed face has her feet worshipped by the immortals. ||1||

To the Kalpalatā of Knowledge— which is skilled in destroying the pain of feet stained by dust, which follows the resonance of sound, whose majesty is expounded in the Vedānta, which bestows the power of debate and other skills,
and which acts as the sun arising from the lotus-face of the Four-faced One (Brahmā)— [I bow].
I worship her who is daily served by the supreme gurus who are masters of knowledge and the ford of liberation. ||2||

I bow to Śivā, whose lotus-face bears a gentle smile, who is bent by the weight of her breasts, the protectress of the three worlds, the destroyer of the hosts of Daityas; she whose breasts surpass the clouds of the rainy season,
and who utterly dispels the suffering of the wretched people submerged in the ocean of worldly existence.
With no other refuge, I ever worship that Śāradā within my heart, the bestower of auspiciousness. ||3||
I bow to her who is an ocean of the nectar of compassion, eternally adorned with armlets and necklaces;
who is the innate consort of the Enemy of Kama (Shiva), whose fame shines upon her lotus-like hands; who is worshipped by Kubera;
who pacifies the host of enemies such as lust and anger; and who bestows the wealth of absolute liberation.
I always worship with devotion in my heart Śāradā, the beloved born from the lotus, who delights the mind. ||4||

Having abandoned other deities, I [worship her] whose heart is pleased by salutation alone— she who is skilled in bestowing the discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal, who is praised by Mukunda and others, who is lauded by the moon-crested Lord Śiva in his ascetic form, and who has made her own disciples true to their vows.
With devotion, I perpetually worship Śāradā within the lotus of my heart. ||5||
Thus ends the "Praise of the Five Jewels of Śrī Śāradā."
